title: Etale direct-image finiteness over quasi-excellent bases
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $B$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, and let $g:V\to T$ be a morphism of finite presentation between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume either that $g$ is proper, or that $T$ is quasi-excellent and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. Here quasi-excellent means that every affine open has a quasi-excellent coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring]. On the ordinary small etale sites, let $Rg_*$ be derived direct image of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves $B_V,B_T$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. In either case, for every bounded constructible complex $K$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], $Rg_*K$ is bounded constructible. If $g$ is proper, there is moreover an integer $d\geq0$ such that $R^qg_*M=0$ for every sheaf $M$ of $B_V$-modules and every $q>d$; this bound is independent of $M$, and the proper case requires neither a ground field nor quasi-excellence nor the invertibility of $\ell$. No bound uniform in $M$ is asserted in the nonproper case.

source.place: Theorem 6.7.1 (Grothendieck, Gabber), printed p.55, with complete Noetherian local ring R=B and maximal ideal zero; the cohomological-dimension clause is kept only for proper g, since for the quasi-excellent alternative Illusie-Laszlo-Orgogozo (literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf), Introduction Theorem 1 and Expose XIII Theorem 1.1.1, give constructibility with a vanishing bound depending on the constructible sheaf, and a uniform bound only for finite-dimensional bases
